name: chan8
algorithm: 8 senders each send 0..n-1 on one channel of capacity 64, and 8 receivers sum what they receive until the senders are done and it is closed; prints the total, 8 * n * (n - 1) / 2. Peers: Go chan; Zig std.Io.Queue (putOne, getOne, close; OS threads, as Zig's std has no tasks). The contended channel of status/std-sync.md (8 senders x 8 receivers, 2M values) as a tools/bench row (std-rewrite, plan/06-m6.md: within 1.25 of Go at 8 carriers).

skip.rust: Rust's std mpsc channel has one receiver; this row needs 8 (std::sync::mpmc is unstable)
skip.mk-wrap: the only arithmetic is the sums, which stay below 2^40

models.zig: OS threads (8 senders, 8 receivers, std.Thread), std.Io.Queue under std.Io.Threaded

no_counts: B24 does not apply: the checksum, the sum of every value sent, shows each value was received exactly once
notes: Concurrency row (B19): logical CPUs 0, 2, ..., 14 (mask 0x5555, eight physical cores), 8 threads, as std-missing/rwlock.
Written by std-rewrite, M6 session 2, 2026-11-08; checksums from the arithmetic.

SRW-RV-2 (2026-11-08, std-rewrite rerun 2 fix round): the Zig cell is added. The row skipped Zig as having no std channel, which is false for Zig 0.17.0: std.Io.Queue(Elem) is a closable many-producer, many-consumer bounded queue with blocking putOne and getOne, and a zero-length buffer is a rendezvous (a getter copies from a parked putter). chan8.zig printed 15992000 at the quick args with capacity 64 and 0, and 249999000000 at 250000 64 and 250000 0 (ReleaseFast, owner's machine, by hand).
